intervals.label: collaboration
intervals.note: No collaboration formation date is published on deap3600.ca, and the INSPIRE experiment record (recid 1108195) carries no date_proposed/date_approved/date_started fields. 2015 is the earliest year for which a dated, sourced account of collaboration activity (planning the detector's commissioning) was found among the sources consulted, and it stands in for an unknown formation date; it is not itself a claim about when the collaboration formed, which is why 'formation' below is null.
intervals.quote: This spring, scientists at SNOLAB will switch on a dark-matter detector that was designed and built at the University of Alberta.

institution_count.note: The older deap3600.ca site (last updated ~Nov 2018) instead says 'over 100 researchers from 25 institutions in 9 countries'; the SNOLAB page's figures are preferred as the more recently confirmed source (accessed 2026-09-17).

member_count.note: The older deap3600.ca site instead says 'over 100 researchers'; the SNOLAB figure is preferred as more recently confirmed (see institution_count note).

name: DEAP-3600 Collaboration
notes: No per-institution membership list is recorded: only aggregate counts were found on deap3600.ca and snolab.ca (checked 2026-10-25 through Internet Archive captures).
No spokesperson or other leadership is recorded here.

summary.plain: The international team that built and runs the DEAP-3600 dark matter detector at SNOLAB in Canada, made up of scientists from institutions in about ten countries.
summary.technical: DEAP-3600 (DEAP) Collaboration: as of the SNOLAB experiment page (read 2026-09-17; an Internet Archive capture of 25 May 2026 shows the same figures), 82 people from 38 institutions in 10 countries; operates the single-phase liquid argon scintillation detector at SNOLAB's 2 km level. No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a formation date.
